applicable_when: The kernel reads in_ptr0 with stride 96 between consecutive x-threads (load address: y0 + 96*x2 + 290400*y1). With XBLOCK=128 threads in the x-dimension, consecutive threads access addresses 96 bytes apart — a stride-96 pattern that causes 10% excessive sectors and only 26.2/32 bytes utilized per sector. This saturates L2 at 96.95% and causes 40.7% of cycles to stall on L1TEX scoreboards. The contiguous dimension of in_ptr0 is y0 (stride-1, the channel axis), but y0 is in the YBLOCK dimension (only 8 threads). Swapping so the channel dimension is in XBLOCK makes loads contiguous and enables 128-bit vectorized loads via tl.max_contiguous/tl.multiple_of hints.
